editor_fail.why: 1) The headline says 'the official count never reached 230 districts' and the body says the official peak is 126. The desk's own notes say an older, wider ministry measure may exist and the rating does not call the figure false. The Home Ministry did use a wider measure around 2009-10 (roughly 220-plus districts in about 20 states with Naxal influence), which matches Modi's 'nearly 20 states'. The headline overclaims, and the 'Mostly true' rating sits oddly with a 230-versus-126 framing. 2) The en and hi seo descriptions say '126 districts and 1,936 incidents in 2010', but 126 is the pre-2018/2014 count, not 2010. 3) list.txt points to content/en|hi/news/ but this story is in content/en|hi/factcheck/. Because of that, the review sheet shows only the slug as the headline, an empty kicker line and no covers, so its overlay cover was never checked. 4) In Hindi the place is spelled करनपुर here but करणपुर in the Rahul Gandhi story, and the claim quote has 'नजदीक 20 राज्यों' instead of 'करीब 20 राज्यों'.
editor_fail.fix: Check the Home Ministry's 2009-10 statements and annual reports for the wider district count. Then reword the headline and finding to say the 230 figure is not in the official 126-district series (not 'never reached'), and revisit the rating if an official figure of about 223 districts is confirmed. Correct both seo descriptions: 1,936 incidents in 2010, peak of 126 districts before 2018. Fix list.txt to use the factcheck paths and regenerate the sheet with headline and covers for review. Standardise the Hindi to करणपुर and करीब 20 राज्यों.
